title: Trump lands in Philippines for ASEAN, Marcos meeting
summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Manila late Tuesday, November 17, to attend a special summit with ASEAN leaders, after skipping the earlier East Asia Summit where the region's leaders…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines (Updated 6:31 p.m.) — United States President Donald Trump arrived in Manila late Tuesday, November 17, to attend a special summit with ASEAN leaders, after skipping the earlier East Asia Summit where the region's leaders touted the value of standing together amid global uncertainty.
Trump, the last world leader to reach the capital, landed at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport as the 49th ASEAN Summit was drawing to a close.

He is set to join Southeast Asian leaders at an ASEAN-US Special Summit, billed as the final engagement of the three-day meetings. He is also expected to briefly sit down on Tuesday evening with the leaders of Australia, India and Japan under the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad.
Trump is also scheduled to meet with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday, November 18, before flying to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
The visit is Trump's first to the Philippines since November 2017, when he attended the ASEAN Summit hosted by then-president Rodrigo Duterte.

The 21st East Asia Summit, held earlier on Tuesday, brought together the 11 ASEAN member states and eight partner countries, among them Japan, China and Russia. Washington has been a full participant in the forum since 2011.

In his opening remarks at the meeting, Marcos said the summit was entering its third decade at a time "when many of the assumptions that have shaped our region are being tested" and "strategic competition has intensified."

"Conflicts within and beyond our region have disrupted energy, food, trade, and supply chains," Marcos said, urging leaders to adhere to international law and prioritize dialogue amid the "upheaval, uncertainty, and unpredictability of our times."

Trump's absence is no surprise as his attendance in the regional meet has fluctuated even in his first term. In 2017, he left Manila without attending the East Asia Summit plenary, citing delays in the program, and then-secretary of state Rex Tillerson represented the United States; Trump said afterward that he had delivered his prepared remarks at a lunch with the other leaders instead.

In Kuala Lumpur in 2025, Trump witnessed the signing of a Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire on the first day of the ASEAN summit but had left for Japan by the time leaders convened for the wider meetings the following day.
Global uncertainty was a recurring theme in ASEAN and world leaders' speeches from the summit's opening day.

Opening the meetings on Sunday, Marcos said geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty, new technologies, climate change and transnational threats were reshaping Southeast Asia "faster than any one country can respond to alone." He said developments in the Middle East earlier this year had put ASEAN nationals at risk and disrupted transport, energy and food supplies across the region.
Much of that disruption traces to the war Trump has waged alongside Israel on Iran, a conflict that Iran retaliated against by blocking trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

The conflict remains unresolved despite attempts at a ceasefire, and Washington has kept a naval blockade and economic pressure campaign against Iran in place. Tehran says it is still waiting for a formal US response to its seven conditions for ending the eight-month war.

With Trump absent for most of the week, other leaders used the meetings to present themselves as advocates of open trade and multilateral cooperation. At Monday's ASEAN-China Summit, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said that although trade restrictions had increased around the world, China, which is ASEAN's biggest trading partner, remained "firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade."
Li also said ASEAN and Beijing should "properly handle differences through dialogue [and] jointly oppose foreign interference" — remarks that can be seen as an apparent swipe at Washington.
Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping during the APEC summit in China.
